## Brazil and Argentina in 9 days: Rio, Iguazu and Buenos Aires

Over **9 days and 8 nights**, you will see [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), Iguazu Falls from both sides and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). There is no flight to the Patagonian glaciers: the itinerary divides its time between two major cities and the waterfalls. This is a convenient introduction to Brazil and Argentina for travelers who want to see their principal sights without a lengthy detour to the south.

A significant feature of this itinerary is that **domestic flights from Rio to Foz do Iguaçu and onward to Buenos Aires are included**, together with transfers, main excursions and dinner with a tango show in the Argentine capital. International flights and optional activities are paid for separately.

## Three main stops and time for a free day

| Part of the route | Highlights |
|---|---|
| Rio de Janeiro | Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado, city center |
| Iguazu | Two national parks, waterfalls |
| Buenos Aires | Sightseeing, tango, free day |

In Rio, you will explore the historic center and ascend [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) via Urca. From the summit, there are views over Guanabara Bay, beaches and the city's surrounding mountains. Another excursion visits the Christ the Redeemer statue on Corcovado. These two viewpoints reveal Rio from different directions, making it easier to appreciate its neighborhoods and coastline.

The journey then moves to the falls. [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) provides wide panoramas, while on the [Puerto Iguazú side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) the trails run alongside individual cascades. Visiting both countries means crossing an international border; the excursion order and access to certain walkways depend on the parks' actual conditions.

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the itinerary includes a sightseeing tour and dinner with a tango show. After the main program, a free day allows time to revisit a favorite neighborhood, walk around Puerto Madero or select one optional outing.

## What can be added, and how much does it cost?

Choose optional activities based on your interests and free time rather than trying to fit every option into one itinerary. The Rio options include:

- “Rio by Night” evening show — **$150 per person**, show-only option.
- Boat trip on Guanabara Bay — **$270 per person**, group tour with at least 2 participants and an English-speaking guide.
- “Secrets of Old Rio” — **$180 per person**, a 4-hour private excursion with a minimum of 2 participants and an English-speaking guide.
- Hang-gliding flight — **$420 per person**, subject to the terms of the separate program.

Other options in Rio include the Botanical Garden, a favela excursion and a helicopter flight. Each should be fitted into an appropriate day and booked under the specific product's conditions. Flying and certain other activities depend on weather and individual participation restrictions.

In Buenos Aires, the free day can be spent in [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) and the northern suburbs, on a gaucho ranch excursion or on a trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). **Uruguay is an optional third country**, not part of the 9-day itinerary's main destinations and not a guaranteed visit. The ferry arrangements and border-crossing requirements for Montevideo must be confirmed separately.

## What does the base price cover?

The tour costs **$2,815 per person** with 3-star, double-room (DBL) accommodation for 2 participants; the rate applies to groups of 1 to 3 people. The package includes the recommended hotels or equivalent properties, airport and hotel transfers with a driver, main excursions, domestic flights along the stated route and dinner with a tango show.

According to the itinerary, excursions in Rio, Iguazu and Buenos Aires have **Russian-speaking guides**, while English-speaking guiding is provided elsewhere. International flights, optional excursions and meals not explicitly listed among included services are excluded. Different optional activities have their own minimum-participant requirements.

When budgeting, separate the core package from voluntary additions. For example, a bay cruise and an evening show can increase personal spending significantly, even though the standard tour already includes excursions introducing Rio.

## Weather and physical demands without Patagonia

Skipping Patagonia reduces long-distance travel and makes packing simpler. Lightweight clothes, sun and rain protection and comfortable shoes for wet walkways are useful in Rio and Iguazu. Buenos Aires weather varies by season, so an extra clothing layer is still sensible. Iguazu paths may include wet sections and steps; access to specific circuits should be checked against official park updates.

One important organizational detail is the transfer day from Iguazu to Buenos Aires. The domestic flight is included in the package, but its actual departure time will determine how much time remains for a walk or rest after hotel check-in.

## What other tour should you compare?

The main alternative is to add Patagonia. The [“Best of Argentina and Brazil in 10 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-brazil-10-days/) visits [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) and El Calafate, but domestic flights are charged separately on that itinerary.

If your priority is **Rio, both Iguazu national parks and Buenos Aires**, the 9-day option covers all three without a glacier leg. If Patagonia matters more than a free day and optional activities, compare the 10-day programs.

## Frequently asked questions about the Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires tour

### Are domestic flights charged separately?

No. The Rio–Foz do Iguaçu–Buenos Aires flights are listed among this tour's included services. International flights are paid for separately.

### Is Montevideo part of the itinerary?

No. [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is a possible optional trip on the free day in Buenos Aires. It adds a third country only if selected separately.

### Is there a free day?

Yes. Day eight is free in Buenos Aires, for independent sightseeing or an optional excursion.

### Is the tango show included?

Yes. Dinner and a tango show in Buenos Aires are included in the package.

## Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay in 13 days: cities, waterfalls and a coastal break

On this tour, **13 days and 12 nights** are divided among three countries so that you see landmark attractions at the beginning and spend several days on the coast toward the end. The journey starts with [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Iguazu Falls from both sides, continues to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and an introduction to gaucho culture, then enters Uruguay via [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) before reaching [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/).

The distinctive feature is **4 nights at the final resort** rather than excursions on every single day. This tour is well suited to travelers who want a mix of active sightseeing and a proper break.

## From Rio to Iguazu: a full opening without a lengthy expedition

The first excursions take place in [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The itinerary covers Corcovado, the city center and Sugarloaf Mountain, an introduction to the city between mountain slopes and the Atlantic. Travelers then head to the waterfalls.

At [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the Brazilian and [Argentine](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) sides are both scheduled. Brazilian viewpoints offer panoramic views of the cascades, while Argentine paths bring visitors closer to the rushing water. As the parks lie in separate countries, the transfer between them requires time for the border crossing.

The sightseeing days here are tightly scheduled. If you want to add the Bird Park or a boat trip, check in advance whether there is enough time between the main excursion, transfer and subsequent flight.

## Buenos Aires, a gaucho ranch and crossing the Río de la Plata

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the program introduces the city, its historic neighborhoods and tango culture. A separate day is spent at the Don Silvano ranch, an important part of the Argentine section: it takes travelers beyond the capital to gaucho traditions and life on the pampas.

The next unusual transition is **a ferry crossing of the Río de la Plata estuary** from Buenos Aires to Uruguay. The first stop is [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), with its small historic center, cobbled streets and lighthouse. It is quite different in scale and appearance from Rio and Buenos Aires.

The crossing is an important part of the route. Allow time at the port for boarding and immigration formalities. Document requirements depend on nationality and must be checked for the travel date; the crossing is not simply a boat outing without border control.

## Why Montevideo and four nights in Punta del Este are included

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) offers a distinct perspective on Uruguay's capital and its urban history. The journey then gradually moves toward [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/), where its final section takes place.

**4 nights** are planned in Punta del Este. Unlike at the start of the trip, there is no need to change city and repack every day. The seaside break provides a slower pace after Rio, the two Iguazu parks and Buenos Aires. When choosing dates, consider the season, weather, wind and preferred coastal activities: beach conditions are not the same year-round.

This balance is particularly attractive to couples or families who want both sightseeing and relaxation. The accommodation format and age-related conditions, however, depend on the actual fare; a resort stay by itself does not imply special family services.

| Stage | Main purpose |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | City and waterfalls |
| Buenos Aires | Tango and gaucho culture |
| Colonia and Montevideo | Uruguayan history |
| Punta del Este | 4 nights of relaxation |

## Included services and easy-to-overlook expenses

The package includes **12 hotel nights with breakfast**, the specified meals, private transfers without a guide and private excursions with a Russian-speaking guide. **Domestic and international flights are paid for separately**, as are entrance tickets to the Iguazu national parks.

Optional excursions, tips, early hotel check-in and late check-out are also charged separately. When comparing prices between tours, use a like-for-like set of services: flights and park tickets can make a substantial difference to the overall budget.

The route ends with a return from Punta del Este to Buenos Aires. International flights should be scheduled around this final leg, rather than assuming the flight home departs from Montevideo.

## Which to choose: Uruguay, Chile or Peru

This 13-day journey emphasizes **the culture of three countries and a final coastal break**. If your priority is more time in capital cities, a visit to the Pacific coast and 12 days without the Uruguayan beach finale, compare the [Brazil–Argentina–Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/).

Travelers wishing to reach the Sacred Valley of the Incas and Machu Picchu after Chile may prefer the [15-day itinerary through four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). It includes more transfers and ends in Peru. The [general multi-country tour catalog](/multi-country/) provides further choices.

## Frequently asked questions about the three-country journey

### Are both sides of Iguazu included?

Yes. The main program includes the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the falls. However, entrance tickets to the national parks are not included in the base price.

### What is the purpose of four nights in Punta del Este?

That part of the route is reserved for relaxing on the Atlantic coast after the sightseeing cities and waterfalls. No packed daily excursion program is specified there.

### Are flights included?

No. International and domestic flights are excluded from the package, although private transfers are included.

### How do travelers reach Uruguay from Argentina?

The journey includes a ferry crossing from Buenos Aires to Colonia del Sacramento and then continues overland through Uruguay.

## VIP tour of Brazil and Argentina: who is the 10-day trip for?

The journey connects three contrasting destinations: [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) on the Atlantic, Iguazu Falls and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). It is especially convenient for a first encounter with both countries, offering their main natural and cultural attractions without additional flights to distant regions.

Main excursions with Russian-speaking guides, transfers and hotel accommodation are included. An executive-class vehicle is used for sightseeing transfers, except in the waterfalls area. At the same time, the private format offers the freedom to select activities on free days; it does not mean all optional excursions are automatically included in the price.

## How the 10 days are arranged

| Days | Main stops |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Rio: city, viewpoints, free day |
| 5–6 | Flight to Iguazu, Brazilian side |
| 7 | Argentine side of Iguazu, flight to Buenos Aires |
| 8–9 | Buenos Aires, tango, free day |
| 10 | Departure from Buenos Aires |

From [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) in Rio, you can see Guanabara Bay and the oceanfront, while Corcovado provides a different view of the city's forested slopes and buildings. Rio's natural landscape, from Tijuca Forest to the sea, has been recognized by UNESCO as cultural heritage.

The free day in Rio can be kept for relaxation or used for a separately booked program. Before heading to the waterfalls, it makes sense not to overschedule and to allow time for packing and the domestic flight.

## Iguazu: why visit both sides of the border?

[Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) are part of the same waterfall system, but offer different experiences. The Brazilian side reveals the full sweep of the cascades; the Argentine side offers upper and lower walkways closer to the water. The main itinerary allocates days to both parks.

For this section, check travel documents and border-crossing rules for each participant's nationality in advance. Access to particular walkways depends on river conditions and the weather. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are optional extras, with their timing, costs and physical demands agreed separately.

## What can be added, and what is included?

Options in Rio include a helicopter ride, a boat trip to islands, the Botanical Garden, caipirinha and churrasco workshops, and trekking. In Buenos Aires, choices include a culinary tour, a gaucho ranch or an independent walk through historic neighborhoods. A trip to Montevideo is also offered: **Uruguay is optional here**, not a third main country.

The basic package includes accommodation, Russian-speaking sightseeing guides and the listed transfers. Domestic and international flights, optional excursions, food and drinks during transfers are charged separately. Hotels may be replaced with properties of an equivalent category if needed.

If the Amazon is a priority, compare the [14-day Brazil–Argentina group tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-group-tour/). To add Chile, explore the [15-day, three-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile/). The 10-day private itinerary suits those who prioritize Rio, both sides of Iguazu and Buenos Aires without expanding the core geography.

## Frequently asked questions about the VIP tour

### Are both sides of Iguazu included?

Yes. Days are reserved for the Brazilian and Argentine sides. Documents and walkway availability are checked before travel.

### Is a helicopter flight over Rio included?

No. A helicopter flight is an optional extra charged separately.

### Can I visit Montevideo?

Yes, as an optional trip from Buenos Aires. It is not part of the mandatory two-country itinerary.

### Is every day filled with excursions?

No. Free time is planned in both Rio and Buenos Aires for rest or separately arranged activities.

## Rio Champions' Parade 2027: a 9-day tour with Iguazu and Buenos Aires

The key date of this tour is **Saturday, February 13, 2027**, the night of the Champions' Parade in Rio de Janeiro. The event features repeat performances by the best samba schools after the competitive Carnival processions. The official LIESA calendar confirms the date, and Ada Tours' itinerary is built around it.

The trip lasts **9 days and 8 nights, from February 12 to February 20, 2027**. You begin with [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and the Sambadrome, then see Iguazu Falls from both sides and end your trip with a tango show in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). It is a good option for travelers who want to combine a specific Carnival event with a complete sightseeing journey through two countries.

## How the 8 nights and main excursions are distributed

| Stage | Nights |
| --- | --- |
| Rio de Janeiro | 3 |
| Foz do Iguaçu | 2 |
| Buenos Aires | 3 |

In Rio, the second day includes a four-hour excursion to [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/), followed by the Champions' Parade that evening. Day three includes [Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue](/brazil/place/corcovado-christ-the-redeemer/). Next comes a flight to the [Iguazu area](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/).

Two sightseeing days are devoted to Iguazu. The Brazilian side offers panoramic views of the cascades, while the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) provides walkways closer to the water. The group then flies to Buenos Aires for a city tour with a Russian-speaking guide, a tango show with dinner and one free day.

## What makes the Champions' Parade special?

During the competitive days, samba schools compete for the results. On Champions' Saturday, the best-performing schools return to the Sambadrome. This makes the trip especially attractive to those who want to experience **the culmination of Carnival week**, rather than only the street celebrations in Rio.

**The Champions' Parade ticket is already included in the tour**, along with a hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfer. The seating category depends on the confirmed ticket; a specific stand or section cannot be assumed from the general tour price. The parade takes place on the evening of day two after a daytime excursion, so factor in the late return and the demands of the next day.

For other [events and festival tours](/interests/events-and-festivals/), the choice works differently: here, the Sambadrome date is fixed. If Carnival is not your main motivation, compare [regular Brazil itineraries](/brazil/tour/) by season and number of transfers.

## How the two days at Iguazu differ

In the Brazilian national park, trails and viewpoints show the broad panorama of the waterfalls. On the Argentine side, some paths run on walkways above the river and beside individual cascades. Two days therefore reveal the complex from different angles rather than repeating the same excursion.

Macuco Safari boat trips, the [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and helicopter flights above the falls are offered separately, each under its own conditions. They should be distinguished from the main excursions already included. The itinerary also offers other independent activities; choices depend on time and budget, while detailed optional-service prices must be checked for the relevant day.

## Buenos Aires finale and an optional third country

In the Argentine capital, the main program includes a city excursion and a tango show with dinner. The separate free day can be spent in historic neighborhoods or on an optional trip to Tigre, a gaucho experience or [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/).

**Uruguay is not part of the main itinerary**: the trip to Montevideo is a separate option. The mandatory journey therefore covers two countries, Brazil and Argentina. Anyone selecting that excursion must consider the cost and documents required for the additional border crossing.

## Included services and rates

The starting price is **from $4,300 per person** in triple accommodation at a 3-star hotel. For double accommodation in the same category, the stated price is **from $4,306**. Options in 4- and 5-star hotels are also offered; rates vary with hotel category and single, double or triple room occupancy (SGL/DBL/TPL).

The package includes hotel accommodation with breakfast, main excursions with Russian-speaking guides, transfers, Champions' Parade tickets and the Sambadrome transfer, plus a tango show with dinner. Unlike some longer itineraries, **the domestic Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires flights are included here**. International flights and optional excursions are charged separately.

The tour combines summer in Rio, the humid waterfall area and another major city. For the evening parade, consider the heat, crowds, late return and the entry rules of the specific ticket. In Iguazu, clothes that can get wet will be useful.

## Frequently asked questions about the 2027 Champions' Parade

### When is the Champions' Parade?

**February 13, 2027.** The date appears on the official LIESA calendar and coincides with the second day of the tour.

### Are the Sambadrome ticket and return transfer included?

Yes. The Champions' Parade ticket and the hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfer are included. The exact section depends on the confirmed ticket.

### Are domestic flights included?

Yes. The Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires flights are included in the listed rates. The international flight is paid for separately.

### Is Montevideo included?

No. The main 9-day journey covers two countries. A day trip to Montevideo is an optional excursion from Buenos Aires on the free day.

## 15-day group tour of Brazil, Peru and Argentina: the 2027 itinerary

This **15-day, 14-night** journey combines three countries and three major experiences: Rio and Iguazu Falls, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), and Argentine Patagonia with Perito Moreno Glacier. The itinerary is designed for **a group of 10 to 20 people in 2027**; specific departure dates are agreed separately.

It is a sightseeing trip with a busy schedule. The tour suits travelers who want to explore natural and historic attractions in several countries within two weeks as part of an organized group. Its distinctive feature is that the route continues from Peru to **El Calafate**, not Chile or Bolivia.

## Brazil: Rio and Iguazu during the first five days

The journey begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), with city sightseeing, Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue, Sugarloaf Mountain and the city's main viewpoints. Dinner without drinks is included on the first day.

After Rio, the group travels to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) to see the falls. The Great Adventure boat excursion and Bird Park are offered as **optional activities**. They should not be presented as part of the main itinerary merely because they are close to the waterfalls.

On day five, the group continues to Peru. This is a substantial inter-country move and should be considered when arranging international flights. All flights on this particular itinerary are paid for separately.

## Peru: the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu

The Peruvian leg starts in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), followed by [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). You will visit [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/), [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/).

A full day is allocated to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Unlike many short multi-country trips, this includes a separate historical and nature-focused stage in the Andes, rather than just a stop in the capital. **Admission tickets to sites on the itinerary are included.**

Lunch in the Sacred Valley is planned for day eight. Other meals should be assessed against the included-services list: the basic package contains hotel breakfasts, but by no means every restaurant meal or drink over the 15 days.

Cusco is situated at altitude, so moving from humid Rio and Iguazu to the Andes requires attention to personal wellbeing. If you have relevant medical conditions, discuss the altitude demands with a doctor beforehand.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires and Perito Moreno Glacier

After Peru, the group travels to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and then south to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). The main natural attraction of the Argentine section is [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in Los Glaciares National Park.

The itinerary includes a visit to the glacier; however, **ice trekking on Perito Moreno is an optional service**. It must not be confused with a standard excursion or viewing the glacier from observation platforms. The activity has its own cost and participation requirements.

The final days are spent in Buenos Aires. After tropical waterfalls, Peru's mountain valleys and Patagonian glaciers, the capital provides an opportunity to explore the city's architecture and atmosphere.

## How the price changes with group size

For 2027, two group sizes and two accommodation options are listed. Rates are **in USD per person**:

| Participants | DBL / SGL |
|---|---|
| 10 people | $3,672 / $5,359 |
| 20 people | $3,486 / $5,172 |

**DBL** means accommodation in a double room; **SGL** means a single room. The lowest price applies to **20 participants sharing DBL accommodation**, not to groups of any size. The program uses **4-star hotels** with breakfast, although equivalent-category properties may be substituted under the tour's conditions.

None of these amounts should be compared with a total travel budget without accounting for flights, as they are excluded.

## What's included and what is paid for separately?

The package includes hotel stays with breakfast, excursions and services according to the itinerary, entrance tickets, private **airport–hotel–airport transfers**, dinner in Rio on the first day without drinks and lunch in the Sacred Valley on day eight.

Despite the group-tour format, airport transfers are private. That does not imply all excursions are conducted privately: each service follows its own stated format.

**International and domestic flights are not included.** Optional excursions, additional food and drinks are also charged separately. Available extras include the Great Adventure at Iguazu, Bird Park and ice trekking on Perito Moreno Glacier.

## How this tour compares with other multi-country options

The strongest reason to choose this route is **Patagonia and Perito Moreno combined with Machu Picchu and Iguazu on a single trip**. Many other three-country combinations focus on cities in Brazil, Argentina and Chile; this itinerary adds Peruvian heritage and a Patagonian glacier.

If you would rather explore the Atacama Desert and the Pacific Ocean instead of a glacier, compare the [12-day Brazil, Argentina and Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/). More options are available in the [multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 15-day group tour

### What is the minimum group size?

The approved rates cover groups of 10 or 20 people. Specific 2027 departure dates are agreed at booking.

### Are flights between countries included?

No. All international and domestic flights are listed as expenses outside the package.

### Is Machu Picchu included?

Yes. The Peruvian leg includes the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu. Admission tickets to the main attractions are included under the program.

### Can I walk on Perito Moreno Glacier?

Ice trekking is listed as an optional excursion and charged separately. The main program includes a visit to the glacier area.
